source_meta._title: You can use bone meal on sea pickles in situations where no sea pickles will grow

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition Minecraft 18w14b in a single-player Overworld world. Use Creative mode for deterministic item acquisition. No particular seed, server, datapack, resource pack, graphics setting, or coordinates are specified. The instructions assume default controls, including E for inventory, number keys for hotbar selection, and right-click for Use Item/Place Block.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make historical snapshot Minecraft 18w14b available, then launch that exact version.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay-affecting mods or datapacks.
A mouse or equivalent input capable of issuing the Use Item/Place Block action is available.
The test location must be dry land: the sea pickle must not be waterlogged or otherwise submerged.
Use an ordinary land block such as grass, dirt, or stone as the supporting block; do not use a coral block.

Creative mode is selected only as a practical way to obtain the sea pickle and bone meal. The report does not require a specific game mode, although it separately notes that bone meal consumption can be noticed in Survival mode.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the affected snapshot selected for this reproduction.
steps.exact_input: Launch the installation configured for Minecraft 18w14b.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays 18w14b as the running version.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode so the required items can be obtained without crafting or exploration.
steps.exact_input: Click Singleplayer -> Create New World; set Game Mode to Creative; then click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Overworld world and Creative flight/inventory access is available.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before manipulating items or blocks.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the player can look and move normally, and the game is no longer displaying a world-loading screen.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and locate the Sea Pickle item through the item-search interface.
steps.exact_input: Press E; open the Search Items tab if it is not already selected; click the search field and type: sea pickle
steps.success_cue: A Sea Pickle item is visible among the search results.

steps.action: Place a Sea Pickle stack into the first hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory and game screen.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the Sea Pickle search result, then left-click hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: A Sea Pickle stack is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search field to locate Bone Meal.
steps.exact_input: Click the search field, replace its contents with: bone meal
steps.success_cue: A Bone Meal item is visible among the search results.

steps.action: Place a Bone Meal stack into the second hotbar slot, keeping it separate from the Sea Pickle stack, and close the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the Bone Meal search result; left-click hotbar slot 2; then press E to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view is restored, with Sea Pickle in hotbar slot 1 and Bone Meal in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Locate an exposed ordinary land block on which to place the test sea pickle. Use the top face of a grass, dirt, or stone block with air above it and no water occupying or touching the intended sea-pickle position.
steps.exact_input: Move and aim at the top face of a suitable dry grass, dirt, or stone block.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at the top face of a dry, non-coral block with enough open space above it for placement.

steps.action: Select the Sea Pickle in the first hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: Press 1.
steps.success_cue: The Sea Pickle is shown in the player's hand and hotbar slot 1 is highlighted.

steps.action: Place exactly one sea pickle on the selected dry land block. Do not right-click the placed pickle additional times, because repeated placement can increase the number of pickles in the same block.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the top face of the selected dry block once.
steps.success_cue: One singular sea pickle is visible on top of the dry supporting block.

steps.action: Confirm that the placed sea pickle is in a condition where normal sea-pickle growth is not being tested: it remains outside water and is not supported by coral. Then select the Bone Meal stack and target the sea pickle itself.
steps.exact_input: Verify that no water occupies the sea pickle's block; press 2; position the crosshair directly over the sea pickle.
steps.success_cue: Bone Meal is shown in the player's hand, hotbar slot 2 is highlighted, and the crosshair is centered on the singular dry sea pickle.

steps.action: Attempt to apply bone meal to the singular sea pickle while it remains on dry, non-coral land. Use one interaction as the minimum deterministic trigger; the original report's unspecified instruction to apply several amounts may be tested by repeating the same input after observation begins.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the targeted sea pickle once while Bone Meal is selected.
steps.success_cue: The Use Item/Place Block input has just been issued while the Bone Meal was selected and the crosshair remained on the dry sea pickle.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked the singular sea pickle once with Bone Meal while the pickle remains on dry, non-coral land. Begin observing the result of that interaction immediately; if repeatability must be checked, issue additional separate right-clicks without altering the placement conditions.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, supporting land-block type, or game mode.
Creative mode and an ordinary grass, dirt, or stone support block are practical execution choices rather than explicit reproduction requirements.

The report says to apply 'several amounts' of bone meal but does not provide an exact number. The plan uses one right-click as the precise trigger and leaves any repeatability attempts to the observation phase.

The report notes that bone meal is consumed in Survival mode, but Survival mode is not required by its listed reproduction steps. This plan uses Creative mode to avoid adding version-sensitive commands or unrelated item-acquisition work.

source_meta._title: Ghost blocks can occasionally be created when placing scaffolding too quickly

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, using the exact affected version Minecraft 1.14 Pre-Release 5. Use an unmodified vanilla client and a single-player Creative-mode test world as the simplest way to obtain enough scaffolding and perform rapid placement safely. A flat world is preferred but is not stated as required by the report. Use a keyboard and mouse, with the Use Item/Place Block action temporarily assigned to an otherwise unused keyboard key.
preconditions: The launcher can start the exact historical version corresponding to the report label Minecraft 1.14 Pre-Release 5.
Use a separate launcher installation or game directory so opening the historical version does not modify unrelated worlds or settings.
No client mods, server plugins, macros, or automatic clickers are active.
A keyboard key that is not assigned to another important action is available for the temporary Use Item/Place Block binding.
The test world contains a level, unobstructed area where a scaffolding structure can be placed and extended.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation for the exact affected version Minecraft 1.14 Pre-Release 5. Do not select the fix version 22w11a or any later version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed and identifies the Minecraft 1.14 Pre-Release 5 installation.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and create a new Creative-mode test world. For simpler positioning, set the world type to Superflat if that option is available; otherwise use a normal world and later find a flat outdoor area. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait before changing settings or placing blocks. Continue only after the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, the player can move normally, and initial world loading is no longer interrupting input.

steps.action: Open the pause menu, select Options, and then select Controls. Locate the control named Use Item/Place Block, which is normally assigned to the right mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Controls
steps.success_cue: The Controls screen is open and the Use Item/Place Block binding is visible.

steps.action: Select the Use Item/Place Block binding and press an otherwise unused keyboard key. Use V if it is shown as unassigned; if V conflicts with another action, use a different unassigned letter key and substitute that key wherever V appears below. Do not use a mouse button for this reproduction.
steps.exact_input: V
steps.success_cue: Use Item/Place Block displays V, or another deliberately selected keyboard key, without an unwanted conflicting binding.

steps.action: Return to the world without restoring the normal right-mouse-button binding.
steps.exact_input: Done -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world and Use Item/Place Block remains assigned to the selected keyboard key.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory action, whose default key is E. Open the Search Items tab, enter scaffolding in the search field, and transfer a stack of Scaffolding to an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E; search text: scaffolding
steps.success_cue: A stack of Scaffolding is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing Scaffolding, using the corresponding number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E, then the hotbar slot number containing Scaffolding
steps.success_cue: The Scaffolding item is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Move to a level, unobstructed patch of solid ground with several blocks of clear space above it. Keep away from walls, trees, or other structures that could intercept placement attempts.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The player is facing an exposed ground block with open space above and around it.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top face of the exposed ground block and briefly tap the remapped Use Item/Place Block key once to place the initial supported scaffolding block. If a key other than V was selected in step 5, use that key instead.
steps.exact_input: Tap V once
steps.success_cue: Exactly one initial scaffolding block is standing on the ground in front of the player.

steps.action: Stand approximately two to three blocks away from the initial scaffolding and aim at an exposed side face of the scaffolding. Position the view so it can be moved upward along the structure as additional scaffolding is placed.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D and mouse movement as needed
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is resting on the side of the scaffolding, the player remains within placement reach, and the scaffolding item is still selected.

steps.action: Press and continuously hold the keyboard key assigned to Use Item/Place Block instead of repeatedly clicking the mouse. While holding the key, keep the crosshair on the exposed side of the scaffolding structure; smoothly move the view upward along the uppermost visible scaffolding as necessary so the game can continue accepting rapid placement attempts. Maintain the uninterrupted placement input for approximately five seconds.
steps.exact_input: Hold V continuously for approximately 5 seconds while tracking the growing scaffolding structure
steps.success_cue: A burst of multiple scaffolding placement attempts has been completed using uninterrupted keyboard input rather than individual mouse clicks.

steps.action: Release the Use Item/Place Block key and immediately stop placing, breaking, walking on, or otherwise updating the resulting scaffolding. Leave the camera facing the structure so the observation subsystem can inspect it before another interaction changes its state.
steps.exact_input: Release V; provide no further interaction input
steps.success_cue: Rapid placement input has ended, the resulting scaffolding structure remains in view, and no subsequent block interaction has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just completed and released a continuous keyboard-driven burst of rapid scaffolding placement, the resulting scaffolding structure is still loaded and visible, and no block has been broken, touched, walked on, or otherwise updated since the burst ended. Begin observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, world type, coordinates, multiplayer requirement, or exact scaffolding arrangement. A single-player Creative Superflat world and a supported vertical scaffolding structure are practical choices intended to remove unrelated resource and terrain constraints.

The report only says to place scaffolding quickly. The vertical rapid-placement path is the simplest implementation of that instruction, but the original attachments may have demonstrated a different placement direction or structure geometry.

The issue is explicitly described as occasional. A single rapid-placement burst may not produce a reproducible candidate every time; if another trial is required, reset to a fresh supported scaffolding block and repeat only the rapid-placement burst rather than modifying the previous structure.

A report comment states that the problem can be reproduced more easily by assigning Use Item/Place Block to a keyboard key and holding that key, so this control configuration is included even though it was not in the original two-line Steps to Reproduce.
Another report comment suggests reproducibility may depend on hardware read/write speed. No specific frame-rate, latency, storage, or hardware condition is established by the report.

The issue metadata lists 22w11a as the fix version. A later comment contains a likely typographical statement referring to 21w11a as fixed, but it also states that versions greater than or equal to 22w11a no longer reproduce; the plan therefore preserves 22w11a as the excluded fix version and recommends the first listed affected version.

source_meta._title: End portals delete blocks that are inside of the portal

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17 Pre-release 3 in a new, disposable, unmodified single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, or server configuration is specified by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Minecraft Java Edition 1.17 Pre-release 3 rather than the fixed snapshot 25w03a or a later version.
Use a new disposable world so that entering the End and modifying gamerules cannot affect a valued world.
Use Creative mode as a practical way to obtain End Portal Frames, Eyes of Ender, and clearly identifiable test blocks without unrelated crafting or exploration.
Enable commands when creating the world so the doTileDrops gamerule can explicitly be set to true, matching the reporter's clarification in the comments.
Use the default interaction control of right-click unless the Use Item/Place Block control has been rebound.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start an installation configured for Minecraft Java Edition 1.17 Pre-release 3. At the main menu, verify the displayed version before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 1.17 Pre-release 3.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, set Allow Cheats to ON, and create the world. Wait until surrounding terrain has rendered and normal movement responds without loading pauses.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player Creative world and can move normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the gamerule command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This explicitly enables ordinary block item drops and removes the incorrect doTileDrops=false condition discussed in the report comments.
steps.exact_input: /gamerule doTileDrops true
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that doTileDrops is set to true.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Select the Search Items tab, search for End Portal Frame, and place a stack in one of the nine hotbar slots along the bottom of the inventory. Search for Eye of Ender and place a stack in a second hotbar slot. Search for Block of Diamond and place a stack in a third hotbar slot. At least 12 frames, 12 eyes, and 9 test blocks are required; extra items in each stack are harmless.
steps.exact_input: E; search: End Portal Frame; search: Eye of Ender; search: Block of Diamond
steps.success_cue: Separate hotbar slots contain at least 12 End Portal Frames, 12 Eyes of Ender, and 9 Blocks of Diamond.

steps.action: Press E again to close the inventory. Select the End Portal Frame hotbar slot by pressing its hotbar number key or scrolling the mouse wheel until the frame is shown in the player's hand.
steps.exact_input: E, then the applicable hotbar number key or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and an End Portal Frame is held in the active hotbar slot, indicated by the highlighted hotbar box.

steps.action: Find or prepare a level area with at least a 5-by-5-block footprint and enough open space to walk around it. The portal will use a central 3-by-3 opening surrounded by frame blocks on its four sides; the four outer corner positions remain empty.
steps.success_cue: A level 5-by-5 area is available with unobstructed access around all four sides.

steps.action: Build an empty End portal frame around a central 3-by-3 opening. Place three End Portal Frames along each of the four sides, for 12 frames total, leaving the four corner positions empty. To obtain the required inward orientation, stand within the central opening while placing each row and face outward toward the row being placed; rotate to face the next side before placing its three frames. Keep all 12 frames at the same elevation.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once for each of 12 frame placements
steps.success_cue: Twelve empty End Portal Frames form four rows of three around a 3-by-3 center; the four corners are empty and every frame's eye socket is oriented toward the center.

steps.action: Select the Block of Diamond hotbar slot. Fill all nine positions of the portal's central 3-by-3 area with diamond blocks. Place them on the supporting ground so that each diamond block occupies the same block layer as the surrounding End Portal Frames, rather than placing the blocks below the frames or on top of them.
steps.exact_input: Applicable hotbar number key, then right-click once in each of the nine central positions
steps.success_cue: Nine diamond blocks completely fill the 3-by-3 interior at the same elevation as the frame blocks, and all 12 frame blocks remain accessible from outside the ring.

steps.action: Select the Eye of Ender hotbar slot by pressing its hotbar number key or scrolling until an Eye of Ender is held.
steps.exact_input: Applicable hotbar number key or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: An Eye of Ender is held in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: From outside the frame, aim at the top of an empty End Portal Frame and right-click to insert an Eye of Ender. Repeat on different frames until exactly 11 of the 12 frames contain eyes. Deliberately leave one known frame empty so portal activation can be performed as a separate trigger action.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once on each of 11 different End Portal Frames
steps.success_cue: Exactly 11 frames visibly contain Eyes of Ender, one frame remains empty, the diamond blocks still occupy the center, and the portal has not activated.

steps.action: Remain outside the portal ring and move to the side containing the one empty frame. Aim the crosshair at the top surface of that empty frame. Do not stand over the central 3-by-3 area, because activation can immediately create the active portal surface there.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is aimed at the final empty End Portal Frame while the player is standing outside the ring and still holding an Eye of Ender.

steps.action: Right-click the final empty End Portal Frame once to insert the twelfth Eye of Ender and activate the completed portal. Do not break blocks, place blocks, run item-removal commands, or change the doTileDrops gamerule after this action.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once
steps.success_cue: The twelfth eye is seated and the completed frame has activated an End portal across the central 3-by-3 area.

steps.action: Immediately move onto the newly activated portal surface using the Move Forward control, W by default; jump with Space if needed to cross the frame edge. Allow the teleport to complete, then wait until the destination terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally. Do not clear the inventory, pick up items deliberately, or execute any commands during the transition.
steps.exact_input: W; Space if needed
steps.success_cue: The player has passed through the newly activated portal, the End dimension has loaded, and normal movement responds without dimension-loading pauses.

stor.handoff_condition: The final Eye of Ender has activated the portal around the test blocks, and the player has passed through it into the fully loaded End without performing any intervening block-breaking, block-placement, item-removal, gamerule-change, or cleanup action. The observation subsystem should now inspect the post-activation state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, coordinates, difficulty, or exact test-block type. Creative mode, a new world, an arbitrary level area, and Blocks of Diamond are practical deterministic choices rather than stated requirements.

The report says to place multiple blocks in the middle but does not specify their number or arrangement. This plan fills all nine cells of the central 3-by-3 area to reproduce the condition unambiguously.

The report comments clarify that doTileDrops was accidentally shown as false in an earlier video and was intended to be true. The plan therefore sets doTileDrops to true explicitly before constructing the portal.

Correct End Portal Frame orientation is required for activation. If inserting the twelfth eye does not activate the portal, at least one frame is facing incorrectly; rebuild the frame while standing in the central opening and facing outward during each placement rather than altering the supplied reproduction condition.

source_meta._title: Standing on top of mud as it converts to clay causes the player to fall through or be pushed out of the block

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w14a in a single-player Overworld using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled for deterministic block acquisition, flight, and game-rule control. Use default controls or the equivalent configured bindings.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to run the exact snapshot 22w14a; do not use the listed fix version, 1.19 Pre-release 5.
Create a disposable Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. No particular seed, biome, coordinates, difficulty, or world-generation type is specified by the report.

The conversion assembly must contain mud directly above an ordinary block, with downward-pointing Pointed Dripstone attached beneath that block. This arrangement is stated in the report and corroborated by the version documentation. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19?utm_source=openai))

Stone is used as the unspecified block below the mud, and Dirt is used only as a temporary construction scaffold. These block choices are practical implementation choices rather than report requirements.
Random ticking will be disabled during construction so the mud cannot convert before the player is positioned. It will be re-enabled at a high value only at the final trigger step.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation configured for snapshot 22w14a. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Java Edition 22w14a
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition 22w14a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, create a new disposable world, set Game Mode to Creative, ensure Allow Cheats is ON under More World Options, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Overworld, can fly, and is permitted to execute commands.

steps.action: Disable random block ticks during construction. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /gamerule randomTickSpeed 0
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that randomTickSpeed is set to 0.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to locate Mud, Stone, Pointed Dripstone, and Dirt. Place each item in a separate hotbar slot, then close the inventory with E. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the game screen.
steps.exact_input: E; search terms: mud, stone, pointed dripstone, dirt; E
steps.success_cue: Mud, Stone, Pointed Dripstone, and Dirt are all visible in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Move to an open, flat area. Select Dirt in the hotbar and construct a temporary vertical pillar four blocks tall. If necessary, double-tap Space to begin Creative flight so each upper face can be targeted and right-clicked.
steps.exact_input: Select Dirt; double-tap Space if flight is needed; right-click to place four Dirt blocks vertically
steps.success_cue: A four-block-tall Dirt pillar stands in an open area with sufficient air beside it for a three-block hanging assembly.

steps.action: While flying level with the top of the temporary pillar, select Mud. Aim at one horizontal side face of the top Dirt block and right-click once, placing one Mud block beside the pillar rather than above it.
steps.exact_input: Select Mud; right-click one side face of the top Dirt block
steps.success_cue: One Mud block is attached beside the top Dirt block, with open air directly beneath the Mud block.

steps.action: Fly below the Mud block, select Stone, aim at the center of the Mud block's underside, and right-click once. This places the Stone block directly below the Mud.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone; right-click the underside of the Mud block
steps.success_cue: The assembly has Mud on top and Stone immediately below it, with no air gap between them.

steps.action: Remain below the assembly and select Pointed Dripstone. Aim at the underside of the Stone block and right-click once so the Pointed Dripstone attaches to the Stone as a downward-pointing stalactite.
steps.exact_input: Select Pointed Dripstone; right-click the underside of the Stone block
steps.success_cue: A downward-pointing Pointed Dripstone is visibly hanging directly beneath the Stone; the vertical order is Mud, Stone, then Pointed Dripstone.

steps.action: Remove every Dirt block in the temporary pillar by left-clicking the Dirt blocks in Creative mode. Do not break the Mud, Stone, or Pointed Dripstone. Confirm that the remaining test assembly is isolated, especially that there are no blocks horizontally adjacent to the Mud block.
steps.exact_input: Left-click each of the four temporary Dirt blocks
steps.success_cue: Only the isolated vertical test assembly remains: Mud above Stone above downward Pointed Dripstone, with air on all four horizontal sides of the Mud.

steps.action: Move above the Mud block using Creative flight. Center the player over it, then hold the descend/sneak control, Left Shift by default, until the player's feet come to rest on the Mud surface. Release Left Shift and release all movement controls. Do not stand on the edge or continue flying.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space if needed; W/A/S/D to center over Mud; hold Left Shift to descend; release Left Shift after landing
steps.success_cue: The player is motionless with both feet positioned on the upper surface of the Mud block.

steps.action: Without moving off the Mud, press T to open chat and type the high-random-tick command exactly. Do not press Enter yet. The value 1000 is a practical high value selected because the report does not provide an exact number.
steps.exact_input: /gamerule randomTickSpeed 1000
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input but has not been submitted; the player remains over the Mud and the block is still Mud.

steps.action: Press Enter to execute the prepared command. Immediately release all movement, jump, flight, and sneak inputs. Remain stationary while the game runs until the Mud directly under the player converts into Clay. Continue only until that single conversion occurs; do not repeat the setup or trigger.
steps.exact_input: Enter; then no movement input
steps.success_cue: The block position immediately beneath the player has just changed from Mud to Clay.

stor.handoff_condition: The isolated Mud block has just converted into Clay while the player was stationary on its upper surface and randomTickSpeed was set to 1000. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before the player intentionally moves, jumps, flies, or sneaks.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, biome, coordinates, or single-player versus dedicated-server requirement. A Creative single-player world with cheats is selected solely to make construction and timing deterministic.
The report says only to place 'a block' below the Mud. Stone is selected as a simple inert full block; the report does not state that Stone specifically is required.
The report recommends a 'high value' for randomTickSpeed but gives no exact value. The plan uses 1000 and records it as a practical inference.
Disabling randomTickSpeed during construction is not part of the report; it is used only to prevent premature conversion and is reversed at the trigger step.
The description says the issue may also affect other entities, but this plan tests the explicitly described player case only.

The description notes an additional possibility when no blocks surround the converting block. The temporary scaffold is therefore removed before triggering, although surrounding air is not stated as necessary for the primary reproduction.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-300781:Copper Golems can open locked chests
source_meta._title: Copper golems can open locked chests without an appropriate key item

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w31a in a fresh single-player Creative mode world with commands enabled. Prefer a Superflat world with structure generation disabled so no unrelated chests can attract the copper golem. Use a separate test world/game directory because this is a historical snapshot. Default controls are assumed: T for chat, E for inventory, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, left-click for normal inventory clicks, and Esc to close a container screen.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly snapshot 25w31a, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 25w36a.
Create a fresh Creative mode world with commands enabled. A dedicated server and additional players are not required by the report.
Use an open test area containing no other copper chests, chests, or trapped chests that could distract the copper golem. The setup commands below clear a 13-by-13 area up to six blocks high.
Keep the player completely stationary while executing the relative-coordinate setup commands in steps 4 through 10. Moving between those commands would cause them to target different locations.
The wooden chest must remain empty so the cobblestone carried by the golem is otherwise eligible to be deposited there.
The area above and around both chests must remain unobstructed so the copper golem can stand beside and interact with them.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for Java Edition snapshot 25w31a, and launch it. If necessary, open the Installations tab, enable snapshot versions, choose 25w31a as the installation version, and use a separate game directory.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu and identifies the running version as 25w31a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands are allowed. For a deterministic empty test area, select Superflat world generation and disable structure generation, then create the world.
steps.success_cue: The player appears in a new Creative mode world with the hotbar visible.

steps.action: Wait before building until world loading has completed. Test that looking and walking respond normally, then stop at one position and do not move until step 10 has been completed.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the player is standing still at the coordinate anchor for the relative commands.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This creates a stone floor one block below the player without changing the player's anchor position.
steps.exact_input: /fill ~-6 ~-1 ~-6 ~6 ~-1 ~6 minecraft:stone
steps.success_cue: A 13-by-13 stone floor exists one block beneath the player, and chat reports that blocks were filled or changed.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command exactly as shown, and press Enter. This removes obstructions from the test area while leaving the stone floor intact.
steps.exact_input: /fill ~-6 ~ ~-6 ~6 ~5 ~6 minecraft:air
steps.success_cue: The space from the player's foot level through five blocks above it is clear throughout the test area.

steps.action: Without moving, open chat and execute the following command to place the copper block that will be used to create the copper golem. It is placed three blocks in one horizontal direction from the player's anchor.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ ~ ~-3 minecraft:copper_block
steps.success_cue: A copper block is visible three blocks from the player.

steps.action: Without moving, open chat and execute the following command to place the copper input chest two blocks to one side of the player's anchor.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~-2 ~ ~ minecraft:copper_chest
steps.success_cue: A single copper chest is visible two blocks to one side of the player.

steps.action: Without moving, open chat and execute the following command to place the target ordinary wooden chest on the opposite side of the player's anchor.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~2 ~ ~ minecraft:chest
steps.success_cue: A single ordinary wooden chest is visible two blocks on the opposite side of the player; the copper and wooden chests are four blocks apart.

steps.action: Without moving, press T and execute the command exactly as shown. The leading slash is required in in-game chat. This merges the report's trial-key item predicate into the lock component of the wooden chest.
steps.exact_input: /data merge block ~2 ~ ~ {components:{"minecraft:lock":{items:"minecraft:trial_key"}}}
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the block data of the wooden chest was modified.

steps.action: Still without moving, execute this command to read back the wooden chest's lock component and verify that the previous command targeted the intended chest.
steps.exact_input: /data get block ~2 ~ ~ components."minecraft:lock"
steps.success_cue: Chat displays a lock value containing the predicate {items:"minecraft:trial_key"}. The relative-coordinate setup is complete, so the player may now move.

steps.action: Perform the report's optional player control check. Open chat and clear the player's inventory so the main hand cannot contain a trial key or any other item.
steps.exact_input: /clear @s
steps.success_cue: All inventory and hotbar slots are empty, including the currently selected main-hand slot.

steps.action: Walk to the ordinary wooden chest and use it once with the empty main hand by aiming at the chest and pressing Use Item/Place Block, which is right-click by default.
steps.success_cue: The chest inventory screen does not appear, confirming that the lock rejects an empty or nonmatching player hand.

steps.action: Press T and give the player one trial key for the matching-key half of the optional control check.
steps.exact_input: /give @s minecraft:trial_key 1
steps.success_cue: A trial key appears in the player's inventory, normally in the first available hotbar slot.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the trial key; if it entered the first hotbar slot, press 1. Confirm that the trial key is visibly held in the player's main hand, then aim at the same wooden chest and right-click it once.
steps.success_cue: The wooden chest's inventory screen is visible while the trial key is held in the main hand, confirming that the configured predicate recognizes the key.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the wooden chest screen without putting any item into the chest.
steps.success_cue: The player has returned to the world view and the wooden chest remains empty.

steps.action: Remove the trial key before beginning the copper-golem portion of the reproduction. Press T and execute the following command.
steps.exact_input: /clear @s minecraft:trial_key
steps.success_cue: No trial key remains in the player's inventory or main hand.

steps.action: Press T and give the player a carved pumpkin for constructing the copper golem.
steps.exact_input: /give @s minecraft:carved_pumpkin 1
steps.success_cue: A carved pumpkin is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Select the carved pumpkin in the hotbar. Walk to the copper block placed in step 6, aim at its top face, and right-click to place the carved pumpkin on top of it. The carved pumpkin must be placed last, after the copper block is already present.
steps.success_cue: A living copper golem is visible at the construction position, with both the copper input chest and the locked wooden chest nearby.

steps.action: Clear the player's inventory so the remaining Creative-mode carved pumpkin cannot be confused with the test item. Open chat and execute the following command.
steps.exact_input: /clear @s
steps.success_cue: The player's inventory and main hand are empty.

steps.action: Give the player one cobblestone. Cobblestone is the chosen nonmatching item because it does not satisfy the report's minecraft:trial_key predicate.
steps.exact_input: /give @s minecraft:cobblestone 1
steps.success_cue: Exactly one cobblestone is present in the player's inventory, normally in the first available hotbar slot.

steps.action: Select the cobblestone's hotbar slot, then walk to the copper-colored chest placed in step 7. Aim at that copper chest and right-click to open its container screen. Do not open the ordinary wooden chest during this step.
steps.success_cue: The copper chest container screen is open, and the one cobblestone is visible in the player's hotbar or inventory section at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Move the cobblestone into the copper chest. With the copper chest screen open, Shift-left-click the cobblestone stack in the player's inventory, or pick it up with left-click and left-click an empty slot in the copper chest's upper inventory grid.
steps.success_cue: One cobblestone is visible in a slot in the copper chest's upper inventory grid, and it is no longer in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press Esc immediately after depositing the cobblestone to close the copper chest, then move a few blocks back without leaving the cleared test area. Do not interact with either chest or with the golem again.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible, both chests and the copper golem can be monitored, and the copper chest contains the cobblestone while the wooden chest remains empty.

steps.action: Wait for the copper golem to search the copper chest and collect the cobblestone. Allow several search cycles if necessary; after failing to find an item, a copper golem may idle before searching again. Do not proceed until the item is visibly carried by the golem.
steps.success_cue: The copper golem is visibly holding the cobblestone, establishing that it has collected the nonmatching item from the copper chest.

steps.action: Continue waiting without interacting. Track the cobblestone-holding copper golem until it reaches the ordinary locked wooden chest, faces or positions itself to use that chest, and begins its item-placement/chest-interaction action. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately when this interaction starts; do not wait to evaluate its outcome.
steps.success_cue: The copper golem is holding cobblestone and has just begun interacting with the locked ordinary wooden chest.

stor.handoff_condition: The copper golem, while visibly holding the nonmatching cobblestone, has just begun its item-placement interaction with the empty wooden chest whose minecraft:lock component requires minecraft:trial_key. Begin observation at this moment without yet classifying whether the chest opens or whether the item is transferred.
uncertainties: The report supplies the lock predicate but not a complete command or chest coordinates. The plan uses relative coordinates and the component-era block-entity command `/data merge block ... {components:{"minecraft:lock":{items:"minecraft:trial_key"}}}` so the predicate is applied without altering its contents.

The report does not specify game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, or server type. A fresh single-player Creative Superflat world with commands and structures disabled is selected as the simplest deterministic environment.

The report says to create a copper golem with a copper chest but does not prescribe crafting, Creative inventory, spawn eggs, or commands. The plan places the copper chest by command and constructs the golem by placing a carved pumpkin on a copper block, matching the affected snapshot's documented creation mechanic.
The report does not name the nonmatching item. One cobblestone is selected as a practical deterministic item that cannot match the predicate requiring minecraft:trial_key.

The optional player lock validation from the report is included because it confirms that the command correctly configured the target chest before the golem interaction. It may be omitted only if a shorter reproduction is required and step 10 successfully returns the intended predicate.
